message.content:
**Yes – you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta, but it’s handled by the city’s enforcement agencies rather than the city council itself.**  
Below is a quick guide on how to do it, what to expect, and some useful contacts.

---

## 1. Understand the City’s Noise Ordinance

| Time | Allowed Decibel Level | Typical Restrictions |
|------|-----------------------|----------------------|
| **10 p.m. – 7 a.m.** | ≤ 55 dB (in most residential zones) | Quiet hours; no loud music, parties, or construction |
| **7 a.m. – 10 p.m.** | ≤ 70 dB (in most residential zones) | Normal day‑time activities allowed, but still limited |
| **Commercial / Industrial Zones** | Higher limits (often up to 80–90 dB) | Different thresholds apply |

> **Tip:** If you’re unsure whether your area is residential, commercial, or mixed‑use, check the city’s zoning map or ask the City of Atlanta’s *Department of Planning & Development*.

---

## 2. Where to File a Complaint

| Method | How to Use | Contact Info |
|--------|------------|--------------|
| **Online 311 Portal** | Visit <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> → “Noise” → Fill out the form. | N/A |
| **Phone Hotline** | Call 404‑656‑4000 (City of Atlanta 311). | 404‑656‑4000 |
| **In‑Person** | Go to the nearest *Public Works* or *Noise Control* office. | 404‑656‑4000 (for directions) |
| **Email** | Send a detailed description to **noise@atlantaga.gov** (if available). | noise@atlantaga.gov |

> **Note:** The city’s *Noise Control* division is part of the *Department of Public Works*. They’ll investigate and enforce the ordinance.

---

## 3. What Information to Provide

1. **Your name & address** (so they can verify the location).
2. **Date & time** of the disturbance.
3. **Description of the noise** (e.g., “loud music from a neighbor’s apartment at 2 a.m.”).
4. **Evidence** (audio recordings, photos, or witness statements).  
   *If you have a recording, attach it to the online form or bring a copy when you call.*

5. **Any prior attempts** to resolve the issue (e.g., talking to the neighbor).

---

## 4. After Filing

1. **Acknowledgment** – You’ll receive a confirmation number via email or text.
2. **Investigation** – A city officer will visit the site (usually within 48–72 hrs).
3. **Resolution** – If the noise violates the ordinance, the officer may issue a warning or citation.  
   *If the problem persists, you can request a follow‑up inspection.*

4. **Appeal** – If you disagree with a citation, you can appeal through the *City of Atlanta Court System* (see <https://www.atlantaga.gov/court>).

---

## 5. When to Contact the City Council

- **Council hearings** are typically reserved for broader community issues (e.g., zoning changes, large‑scale noise complaints affecting multiple residents).  
- If you feel the city’s enforcement isn’t addressing repeated violations, you can bring the matter to your **local council member**.  
  - Find your council member here: <https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/council>  
  - Call their office at the number listed on the page.

---

## 6. Quick Checklist

- [ ] Identify the exact location (address or intersection).
- [ ] Record the noise (if possible).
- [ ] File the complaint online or call 311.
- [ ] Keep the confirmation number.
- [ ] Follow up if you don’t hear back within a week.

---

### Final Thought

While the city council doesn’t directly handle noise complaints, they can advocate on your behalf if you feel the city’s enforcement is inadequate. For most cases, the *Noise Control* division will be your first point of contact. Good luck, and hope the noise stops soon!
